newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher on budget speculation.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher on budget speculation.

text.p: Delhi shares closed higher on Monday on reports that the government will allow firms to buy back their shares and have non-voting shares under a proposed law, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 4.48 points higher at 756.03 points.

The Economic Times newspaper reported on Monday that the draft of a new Companies Bill proposed to double the investment limit of companies in other firms to 60 percent from 30 percent allowed under the present company law.
The newspaper also said companies would be allowed to buy back their shares and non-voting shares would also be allowed under the new law being drafted by the government.

"Despite a rise in stock prices the fate of the market would depend on the ensuing budget as buyers have been expecting some favourable proposals for the capital market," said Satish Gera of brokers DSJ Finance Corporation Ltd.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to present the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget on February 28.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and domestic financial institutions made heavy purchases of blue chips, brokers said.

Brokers said sepculation that financial institutions may be allowed to raise their stake in the State Bank of India, India's largest commercial bank, to 24 percent from 20 percent, drove the bank's shares up 7.55 rupees to 296.30.
TISCO rose 2.05 rupees to 199.75 on anticipation of budgetary incentives to the steel industry, brokers said.
Reliance fell 1.15 rupees to close at 277.25.
Arvind Mills gained 2.25 rupees at 140.50 on buying by FIIs and mutual funds.
